title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
gist: METR's updated time horizon report adds longer and more open-ended, judgment-heavy tasks. It finds that AI capability on verifiable tasks such as coding is still growing exponentially, but models still fall short of humans on research-taste tasks like designing AI evaluations. That gap is central to how close automated AI R&D really is, although newer models such as Opus 5.5 are starting to reach 'borderline above the bar' results.

insights.claim: METR's original time horizon plot rated AI models by the length of tasks they could complete, with each task's difficulty measured by how long human testers took to finish it. It showed the length of tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubling every four months.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: A four-month doubling of agentic task length is a key benchmark that bulls use to justify AI capex and to argue that labor automation is coming soon.
insights.quote: every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled

insights.claim: METR's updated time horizon report finds that some AI capabilities are still improving on an exponential trajectory. It also indicates that models are weaker at tasks that require judgment than they are at coding.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: The data supports the coding-agent investment thesis but warns against assuming the same gains in judgment-heavy knowledge work.
insights.locator: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR

insights.claim: The METR time horizon plot was widely shared and widely misinterpreted because the measures behind it are complex.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Treat headline time-horizon numbers with caution; the metric is easy to over-read in either direction.
insights.quote: which was widely shared—and widely misinterpreted, due to the complexity of the measures it used
insights.locator: The report is an update to

insights.claim: The updated METR task suite adds tasks estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, plus more open-ended tasks. Because paying people to complete tasks lasting hundreds of hours is too expensive, most human completion times in the new report are estimates rather than measurements.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Long-horizon data points on the new plot rest on estimated baselines, so the extrapolated trend is less certain than it looks.
insights.quote: the completion times are mostly estimates
insights.locator: In the new report, however, the completion times

insights.claim: AI systems have become very good at coding and math because reinforcement learning works well where success can be checked automatically. It is much harder to apply to tasks where success is poorly defined or slow to determine, such as choosing a new research direction.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Expect automation to arrive first in domains with automatic verifiers, such as software and math. Domains without verifiers face a structural lag.
insights.locator: We know how to teach neural networks

insights.claim: A central open question in AI is how far progress on automatically verifiable tasks carries over to tasks where success is hard to measure. Those harder tasks are exactly the ones needed for AI systems to automate research and development.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Whether gains on verifiable tasks transfer to other tasks is the swing factor for timelines to recursive self-improvement and for the value of the AI labs.
insights.locator: One of the biggest questions in AI right now

insights.claim: Sayash Kapoor of UC Berkeley thinks research taste, meaning the ability to choose promising questions, hypotheses and experiments, will be a major bottleneck to automating AI R&D. Others argue that models trained on easy-to-verify tasks will eventually handle open-ended tasks too.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Expert disagreement about transfer means timelines for automating AI R&D are still highly uncertain, both upside and downside.
insights.locator: Still, people disagree about how to interpret

insights.claim: OpenAI reported in a blog post that its models perform worse on the real-world tasks its employees ask them to do than on the easier, more verifiable tasks in METR's original suite.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: A lab is admitting a gap between benchmark and real-world performance, which suggests enterprise productivity gains may come in below what benchmarks imply.
insights.locator: And in a Wednesday blog post, OpenAI reported

themes.theme: Models vs. humans on open-ended tasks

insights.claim: In a METR task where models designed new AI evaluations that METR staff then scored, none of the AI-designed evaluations was good enough for METR to consider useful for its research. This happened even though the most advanced models now beat almost every human at software engineering.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Being superhuman at coding does not yet mean being able to do research, which caps near-term claims about AI R&D automation.
insights.quote: Not one of the AI-designed evaluations was good enough for METR employees to consider it useful for their research.
insights.locator: METR researchers have worked to incorporate

insights.claim: Models also fell short of human performance on a METR task that asked them to score philosophical arguments, which is meant to capture good judgment. METR staff disagree about how relevant the task is to automating AI R&D, and most arguments were rated by a single person.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Signals about judgment are weak and noisy; don't overweight them in either direction.
insights.locator: In another task, models have to score philosophical arguments

insights.claim: Models are improving on open-ended work. Newer models such as Opus 5.5 tend to reach METR's "borderline above the bar" rating on evaluation-design tasks, while a year ago every model scored "clearly below the bar".
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Progress on judgment-heavy research tasks within one year is an early sign of the open-ended capability that matters most for AI R&D automation.
insights.quote: Just a year ago, every model was scoring in the “clearly below the bar” category.
insights.locator: Even if the models do lag behind

insights.claim: In an August preprint, Sayash Kapoor and collaborators reported that AI models cannot yet reproduce human computer science research on their own.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Independent research supports the view that autonomous AI research has not arrived yet.

insights.claim: Earlier this month, a separate and heavily redacted METR report claimed that AI might be doubling the pace of AI capabilities progress at Anthropic. It raised fears that Anthropic, which just had a blockbuster IPO, could soon reach full recursive self-improvement.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Claims that AI is speeding up AI progress at a newly public lab could drive both investor enthusiasm and regulatory or safety scrutiny of Anthropic.
insights.quote: AI might be speeding up the pace of AI capabilities progress at Anthropic by a factor of two
insights.locator: Parts of the AI community are still reeling

insights.claim: METR's Matt Putz expects that trends on hard-to-verify, judgment-laden tasks will never be as clean and robust as trends on easy-to-specify tasks. The new report includes few such tasks because they are so hard to design and score.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: The capability that matters most for AI R&D automation will stay the hardest to forecast, so expect a lasting uncertainty discount on long-range timelines.
insights.quote: Ultimately, I don’t think we’ll be able to establish trends as clean and robust as for the easy-to-specify [tasks].
insights.locator: Matt Putz, a member of the technical staff

insights.claim: Najoung Kim of Boston University says the improvement on open-ended tasks says something about the present, but it is unclear how to extrapolate it.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Be careful about extrapolating the open-ended task results into forecasts.
insights.quote: I’m not sure just yet how to think about how it would extrapolate.

insights.claim: Experts see METR's move toward creative, open-ended evaluations as a step in the right direction but agree the field is still far from definitive answers on whether, and how fast, automated AI R&D will arrive.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Demand for new, harder evaluations is growing, and that is an opportunity for evaluation and benchmarking organizations.
insights.quote: We’re at the point where AI evaluations need to get more creative
insights.locator: Though it’s difficult to score these new tasks
